title: EOMasters Newsletter #016
description: A hand-picked selection of news from the field of EO and RS
html:
EOMasters Newsletter #016

28/01/2024

Hello EO-Masters!

I would like to know a little about you as my dear readers.

I'm interested in what you are currently working on. You might work on your thesis, or you develop a specific algorithm, or you are doing a temporal analysis. Let me know what you are doing.

Of course, I also share what I do with you.

I'm currently creating a coastal map at a global scale and at 10m resolution. The map will indicate land and water, the coastline, intertidal areas and more. It will be made available in the month to come.

Please fill your answer in the provided questionnaire.

Ciao

Marco

EO and RS News

Sentinel-3 Hydro-Cryo Validation Report is Available

From March to October 2023, a full mission reprocessing was carried out using the new thematic processors. The purpose of the Validation Report is to report the validation performed on the reprocessed data set, verify data quality, and report to end users. The publication also describes the results obtained with the new Hydro-Cryo Thematic Products.

  • Validation Report for Sentinel-3 Hydro-Cryo full mission reprocessing is now online

NovaSAR-1 Announcement of Opportunity: ESA encourages S-band applications

NovaSAR-1 is a small radar satellite developed in the UK, operating at S-band frequency. One key application area of the S-band is agricultural monitoring. Other applications include flood monitoring, forest monitoring, land cover classification, disaster management and maritime applications.

ESA is now offering possibilities to develop new applications in the S-band microwave frequency range, with a new Announcement of Opportunity for NovaSAR-1 data. You can submit your proposal until 20 December 2024.

  • ESA encourages S-band applications with NovaSAR-1 Announcement of Opportunity

An in-depth look at the Copernicus Energy Thematic Hub

The Energy Hub is a platform that provides data and information on energy-related topics, such as renewable energy sources, climate variables, and electricity demand.

The data allows users to explore historical and projected data on various parameters that affect the suitability of locations for renewable energy investment, such as wind speed, solar radiation, and temperature.

  • OBSERVER: An in-depth look at the Copernicus Energy Thematic Hub

Sentinels and AI reveal 75% of fishing vessels not tracked

The study used five years of data from the Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 missions, along with GPS information, to identify vessels that had not reported their positions. It also applied machine learning to the data to determine which vessels were fishing. This analysis identified 'dark fleets' of fishing vessels that were not being tracked by public tracking systems. This 'dark fleet' makes up to 75% of the world’s industrial fishing vessels.

The study helps to understand the scale and impact of human activity at sea, and to address issues such as illegal fishing.

  • ESA - Sentinel-1 and AI reveal 75% of fishing vessels not tracked

  • Release GeoTools 30.2

Beyond EO

Can Submerging Seaweed Cool the Climate?

The article discusses the potential of growing and sinking seaweed to mitigate climate change by storing carbon at the bottom of the ocean. The challenges and uncertainties associated with this strategy will be discussed, such as the optimal locations, methods, and effects of seaweed cultivation. The page further provides some global and local perspectives on seaweed strategies, such as the ethical, economic, and social implications for different regions and communities.

  • Can Submerging Seaweed Cool the Climate?

That's it for this issue. I hope you enjoyed this collection of news. Stay tuned for the next edition, which will arrive in your inbox in about two weeks.

Tschüss and Goodbye!

Marco
